newsitem.title: USA: Maxwell House cuts coffee prices by 30 cents a can.
newsitem.headline: Maxwell House cuts coffee prices by 30 cents a can.

text.p: Maxwell House Coffee Co, a division of Philip Morris Co's Kraft Foods, said on Thursday the company will cut the list price of its standard 13-ounce cans of ground regular and ground decaffeinated coffees by 30 cents due to the decline in prices on the world's futures markets.
The decrease, which will take effect September 8, brings the price for a standard 13-ounce can of regular ground to $3.06, and decaffeinated ground Maxwell House to $3.76, the spokeswoman said.

Maxwell House's retail price decreases come on the heels of an identical price cut on Tuesday by Procter and Gamble Co unit Folgers Coffee Co. Folgers is the largest roaster in the U.S. followed by Maxwell House.

Both roasters had been forced to raise the retail price of a 13-ounce can of ground coffee four times since the beginning of the year, from $2.41 to $3.36 to reflect the soaring cost of green coffee on the world's futures markets.
But since surging to 20-year highs in late May, the price of green coffee on New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange has slipped some 40 percent.
The spokeswoman said, however, the list prices of Maxwell House Instant Coffee, Maxwell House single packets of coffee and General Foods International flavored coffees will remain unchanged.
((-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk, +1 212 859 1640))
